title: Lane Weave Playmap: Quarterly Roadmap for Hosted API & Model Catalog
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Objective: Produce a prioritized, risk-aware quarterly plan that aligns Hosted API landing pages, model catalog rotations, and canary corridors so we can increase throughput predictability and reduce customer-facing regressions during model swaps.

Context: The hosted model catalog continues to grow rapidly. Teams need a predictable, low-drift cadence for introducing model variants, rolling out quantized builds, and retiring legacy tiers. This ticket captures the playmap (lane-weave) that stitches: capacity hedges, quality gates, rollout canaries, and developer-facing docs.

Scope (Q2):
- Define 'commit lanes' (steady, surge, and experimental) for model onboarding and endpoint promotions.
- Set canary corridors with automatic rollback thresholds and observability hooks (latency, error-rate, hallucination-regressions).
- Establish a coordinated release calendar with Dedicated capacity reservations for high-throughput cohorts.
- Ship a cross-functional playbook: PRD + runbook + Console dashboard widgets for per-route model health.

Out-of-scope: Full pricing redesign, Private/VPC deploy automation (tracked separately).

Acceptance criteria:
- Commitment lanes documented and approved by Eng, SRE, and DevEx.
- Canary automation (simple threshold rollback) demoed in staging and verified in canary simulation.
- Roadmap published to Confluence with per-milestone owners and release windows.

Trade-offs considered:
- Faster rotation cadence improves access to better models but increases regression risk and operational overhead. We prioritize a conservative cadence for high-SLA customers and a faster experimental lane for early adopters.
- Aggressive autoscaling reduces latency during surges but increases unit cost; recommend burst-only autoscaling for experimental lanes.

Deliverables:
- Lane-weave playbook (PRD) + Confluence page link.
- Calendar with coordinated canary windows and Dedicated capacity reservations.
- Console widget spec for model health and token-cost deltas.
- Eval set and prompt-suite for Canary and Staging runs.

okrs: OKR-1: Increase model rotation velocity while keeping model-related customer incidents <= 2 per quarter
OKR-2: Reduce time-to-detect regressions in canaries from 48h to <12h via alerting and structured evals
OKR-3: Improve per-route cost transparency so engineering teams can choose cheaper compatible variants when appropriate
risks: Regression risk when swapping models for high-SLA endpoints
Insufficient telemetry coverage for hallucination/regression signals
Capacity conflicts between Dedicated reservations and ad-hoc surge requests
